intro.en: The body in detail, the things it does on its own, and the verbs for postures and gestures.

texto.en:
**The face.** **La frente**, **las cejas**, **las pestañas**, **las mejillas**, **la barbilla**. With age come **las arrugas** and **las canas**.

**Inside.** **El cerebro**, **el corazón**, **los pulmones**, **el hígado**, **los riñones**, **el estómago**, **el intestino**. The frame: **el esqueleto**, **la columna**, **las costillas**.

**Postures.** Spanish separates the movement from the result:

- Movement, with a reflexive verb: **sentarse**, **tumbarse**, **agacharse**, **levantarse**, **ponerse de pie**, **ponerse de rodillas**.
- Result, with **estar** or **quedarse**: **estar sentado**, **estar tumbado**, **estar agachado**, **estar de pie**, **quedarse quieto**, **quedarse dormido**.

So **me senté** means I sat down, and **estaba sentado** means I was sitting. English uses sit for both.

**Position.** **De pie**, **de rodillas**, **de espaldas**, **de perfil**, **de frente**, **boca arriba**, **boca abajo**.

**What the body does.** **Bostezar**, **estornudar**, **toser**, **sudar**, **temblar**, **masticar**, **tragar**. What comes out: **el sudor**, **las lágrimas**, **la saliva**.

**With the hands.** **Acariciar** a un gato, **rascarse** la cabeza, **arañar**, **aplaudir**, **señalar** con el dedo, **cruzar los brazos**, **dar una patada**, **dar un puñetazo**.

The body takes the article, not the possessive: **se rascó la cabeza**; **cruzó los brazos**.

frases.es: Los expertos aseguran que más de la mitad de lo que comunicamos no pasa por las palabras.
frases.en: Experts claim that more than half of what we communicate does not go through words.
analisis: más de la mitad de lo que comunicamos

frases.es: Quien cruza los brazos durante una conversación suele estar a la defensiva, aunque no lo sepa.
frases.en: Someone who crosses their arms during a conversation is usually on the defensive, even if they don't know it.

frases.es: Rascarse la cabeza o tocarse la barbilla indican duda, mientras que levantar las cejas expresa sorpresa.
frases.en: Scratching one's head or touching one's chin show doubt, while raising the eyebrows expresses surprise.

frases.es: Hay gestos que no podemos controlar: bostezamos cuando nos aburrimos y sudamos cuando tenemos miedo.
frases.en: There are gestures we cannot control: we yawn when we are bored and sweat when we are afraid.

frases.es: En una entrevista de trabajo conviene quedarse quieto, sentarse derecho y mirar de frente.
frases.en: In a job interview it is advisable to keep still, sit up straight and look straight ahead.

frases.es: Sin embargo, los gestos no significan lo mismo en todas partes.
frases.en: However, gestures do not mean the same everywhere.

frases.es: Señalar a alguien con el dedo, por ejemplo, es normal en algunos países y de mala educación en otros.
frases.en: Pointing at someone with your finger, for example, is normal in some countries and rude in others.
analisis: Señalar a alguien con el dedo

pregunta.en: According to the text, what do crossed arms usually show?

bloques.correcta: That the person is on the defensive

pregunta.en: According to the text, pointing with a finger is…

rude everywhere.en: It is normal in some countries.

a sign of doubt.en: Doubt is shown by scratching one's head.

pregunta.en: Complete: I sat down and stayed there for an hour.

bloques.frase: Me senté y estuve ___ una hora.

sentándome.en: That would be the movement, which takes a second.

sentarme.en: After estuve you need the participle.

pregunta.en: Which verb describes what you do when you are sleepy?

la.en: With the body, the article: the reflexive already says whose it is.

su.en: Spanish uses the article with parts of the body.

bloques.frase: Se agachó para recoger las llaves.

texto.en: He bent down to pick up the keys.
He hurried to pick up the keys.
He was sitting to pick up the keys.

bloques.frase: Me quedé dormido en el sofá

traduccion.en: I fell asleep on the sofa.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Describe a person from head to toe as a novelist would: face, body, posture and gestures.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud what certain gestures mean in your culture and which ones are rude.
